subject: Renewal restructure: multi-year ramp + co-term request
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@atlashealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: term rework + ramp smoothing request

Connor —

Hope you had a great weekend. We're starting our internal planning for the Aug 31 renewal with Redwood and have a couple of asks that came out of leadership and finance. High level: AtlasHealth is open to a 3-year term, but we need a gentler CPU/token ramp in year 1 and a co-term with our other vendors on 2028-01-01. Specific asks: 

- Multi-year: 36 months preferred, but with a % growth cap in year 1 (no more than +30% compute over current run rate)
- Ramp smoothing: front-loaded credits or a staggered burst schedule so monthly overages are predictable
- Auto-renew opt-out window: finance requires an opt-out notice 60 days before renewal rather than 30
- Co-term: want contract end date 2028-01-01 to align with other platform contracts

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a staggered ramp (monthly tranches) and either credits or a pre-bought burst bucket? If so, procurement wants a draft amendment and cost estimate by next Tuesday (8/31).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Sarah Bennett
Head of Platform Ops | AtlasHealth
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: term rework + ramp smoothing request

Thanks Sarah — really useful detail. Short answer: yes, we can structure a 36-month term with a ramp smoothing mechanism and move the co-term date, but there are a few knobs to align on (credits vs burst buckets vs staged monthly tranches).

High-level proposal we can get you by 8/31: 
- Option A (Credits): front-load X credits that offset first 3 months of higher token spend; after credits are exhausted regular unit pricing applies.
- Option B (Staged burst bucket): pre-purchased burst capacity usable across months with overage protection; unused burst can be prorated or applied as credits for year 2.
- Co-term handling: we can set an explicit contract end-date of 2028-01-01 and prorate year 1 price to align cost to that boundary.
- Auto-renew window: we can extend opt-out to 60 days in the amendment.

Karthik/Marissa — looping you in to confirm pricing mechanics and whether we should propose a floor/true-up cadence quarterly or monthly. Sarah — would a short spreadsheet with year-by-year token bands plus a burst-credit scenario be the most helpful?

I can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

—Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Pricing notes for AtlasHealth renewal (internal)

Connor / Marissa — quick internal note based on Sarah's asks. I ran a couple of scenarios against their current run rate (we have usage history in the HS deal). Proposed structure to reduce friction: 

- Year 1: 36-month term but prorated year 1 to end on 2028-01-01 (so year 1 is ~4 months shorter if we align start today). We should present both a prorated and non-prorated view.
- Ramp smoothing: propose a 3-tranche monthly schedule for the first 6 months: 40% / 70% / 100% of target tokens, with an optional burst bucket of 250,000 tokens. Burst bucket priced at 0.75x standard overage rate; unused bucket converts to credit at 50% value after 12 months.
- Floor & true-up: quarterly true-up to avoid surprises; apply overage protection so small spikes don't immediately cascade to higher tiers.
- Auto-renew: extend notice to 60 days, but add a mutual-exit clause if usage falls below 40% of contracted baseline for two consecutive quarters.

Attachments: I put a draft ramp schedule spreadsheet together (ramp_schedule_v2.xlsx) and a short amendment template (renewal_amendment_draft.pdf). I'll drop both to the thread — Connor, please review numbers and decide which option (Credits vs Burst) to present; Marissa, we'll need your sign-off on the legal language re: prorate/co-term.

-Karthik
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
